newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CBOT/LIFFE link up aims to entice HK investors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT/LIFFE link up aims to entice HK investors.

text.p: Hong Kong investors will be able to trade U.S. Treasury bond and German Government bond futures and options more easily because of a link agreement between the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) and the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), LIFFE said.

"The link agreement will mean that, for the first time, investors in Hong Kong can trade both these contracts, using open outcry, during much of their regular business day," LIFFE spokesman Richard Pratt said in a statement on Monday.

From May 9 LIFFE bund futures and options would be traded on the CBOT for nearly three hours during Hong Kong's morning, and CBOT futures and options on the U.S. long bond would be traded for five and a half hours during Hong Kong's afternoon and early evening.
Akio Shimizu, managing director CBOT Asia-Pacific, said the agreement would keep the electronic trading systems of CBOT and LIFFE well positioned to improve open outcry markets.
"I have no doubt that investors in Hong Kong will be quick to grasp these opportunities" Shimizu said.
Pratt told Reuters that feedback from LIFFE members in the region indicated that their Asian business was growing.
"Those investors here in Hong Kong and the rest of the region who have European assets are looking at a time of increasing uncertainty in Europe," said Pratt.
If they increased their European assets in the runup to European Monetary Union on January 1, 1999, they would need to hedge their positions, he said.
LIFFE was currently discussing a possible linkage with Singapore International Monetary Exchange, said Pratt, declining to give further details.
